FIRST EXPERIMENT / NOT AN OPERATIONAL FORECAST

Does the extra data help?

Average error on the later, held-out observations. Shorter bars are better.

Observed level (teal) and experimental prediction (orange) on the held-out period. Every prediction uses earlier observations. This is a historical replay, not a forecast of what happens next.

How this experiment works & what it cannot prove

This short record is not evidence of reliable flood warnings. A single local rain gauge does not represent the Severn catchment. Historical publication delays and data revisions are not reconstructed, so real-world performance may be worse. Overlapping forecast horizons make errors dependent; these are descriptive scores, not confidence estimates.

Next: longer quality-checked archives, several flood events, catchment rainfall, reporting-delay checks and rolling time-based validation.

THE QUESTION WORTH TESTING

Can we see a rise
coming sooner?

Can rainfall and upstream river levels improve forecasts at Diglis, compared with simply assuming the latest level will stay the same?

We’ll measure the improvement before making any claims.

  1. 01 / NOW

    Build a trustworthy observation desk

    Real readings, timestamps, missing-data checks and downloadable evidence.

  2. 02 / NEXT

    Assemble the historical record

    Upstream and local rainfall snapshots are connected. Longer quality-checked archives are the next step.

  3. 03 / THEN

    Test a small forecasting experiment

    Inspect the first 1, 3 and 6-hour holdout comparison above. High-water event validation is still outstanding.

Small scope. Clear evidence.

What the numbers mean

Stage is height relative to a local reference point. It is not river depth or height above sea level. Levels from different gauges cannot be directly compared as if their reference points were identical.

What’s working today

A live Diglis view plus saved multi-station history and an export. An exploratory historical comparison now includes upstream and local rainfall observations. No background collection, notifications or validated operational predictions. Refresh requests the latest available data while this page is open.

How we’ll judge progress

First, forecast error against a simple baseline. Later, missed high-water events, false alarms and lead time using an explicitly defined research threshold. No accuracy claims until we have tested them.

This uses Environment Agency flood and river level data from the real-time data API (Beta). This uses Environment Agency rainfall data from the real-time data API (Beta).
